analysis: Only CHANGELOG.md was supplied, as full head text with no diff markers, so I could not tell which entries this PR added. No code or config changes were available to check, so I report no concrete security regression. Several entries touch the T-041 SSD prefix-cache area; they are claims about code I did not see. (1) The top 'demanded prefix reuse' entry says the demanded shared-prefix checkpoint is kept beside the deepest one, authenticated repeated checkpoints get the reserved SSD write share on first local appearance, and one aligned boundary is captured in dense Qwen prompts below the solo stripe. T-041's per-donation gate (adoption bound plus 1,024-token benefit floor, SSDPrefixCache.donate) and the 30-minute TTL, HMAC lookup tags and account-scoped cacheSalt must still hold. A reviewer of the provider code should confirm the new capture path does not widen the at-rest surface, add prompt-derived metadata beyond the keyed lookupTag, or let a co-tenant force writes of a victim's prefix. Cache salt is coordinator-authored from the authenticated account, so cross-account reuse should remain closed (SEC-035 is the accepted same-account TTFT oracle). The 'raise SSD write budget to 750 GB/day' entry is not described in T-041 and is a minor threat-model gap. (2) The Autopilot entries (protocol 3, live lease, shadow by default) and the provider 0.9.16 and 0.9.17 entries relate to TB-002 and TB-011. They claim the lease is acknowledged and that observation-only mode adds no commands. These could not be checked without source. (3) The advisory PR review and budgeted-scan entries add workflow and funding surface outside the threat model scope. (4) Payout, Stripe and Global Payouts migration entries touch TB-008, T-030 and T-031. The T-031 removal of the unauthenticated earnings lookup is described as a security fix and consistent with the model. No contradiction with the canonical threat model is visible from the changelog text alone.
